title: ABM retargeting: how to reach the right people, not just the right accounts
summary: ABM retargeting should reach named buyers inside target accounts, not anyone who touched the site. See standard vs account-level vs contact-level retargeting.
body_markdown:
ABM retargeting means re-serving ads to the specific, qualified buyers inside your target accounts — not to anyone who happened to touch your site, and not to a company as an anonymous whole. That one distinction is where most retargeting spend leaks. Standard retargeting chases every prior visitor regardless of fit. Account-level retargeting reaches the right logo but can't tell you which person. The point of ABM retargeting is to reach the right *people* .


Get that right and retargeting stops being a tax on brand traffic and starts being a way to stay in front of live buyers. Here's what ABM retargeting is, how it differs from the retargeting you're probably running, and how to do it at the contact level.


## What ABM retargeting actually is


**ABM retargeting is retargeting scoped to named, qualified contacts inside your ICP and target accounts.** Instead of re-serving ads to everyone who visited a page, you re-serve them to the specific buyers who fit your ICP and belong to accounts you're actually pursuing. Generic retargeting chases anyone who's been to your site; contact-level retargeting focuses only on known, qualified contacts. It's a contact-level motion, not just an audience filter you bolt onto a standard retargeting campaign.


The difference matters because most B2B site traffic is off-ICP — job seekers, competitors, existing customers, students. Retarget all of them and you pay to follow people who will never buy. Retarget the named buyers inside your target accounts and every impression works toward pipeline.


## Standard vs account-level vs contact-level retargeting


There are really three tiers of B2B retargeting, and they reach very different people:


- **Standard retargeting** — re-serves ads to anyone who touched the site. Simple, and mostly aimed at people outside your ICP.
- **Account-level retargeting** — narrows to visitors from target accounts, usually by IP or company match. Better, but it reaches "someone at Acme" without telling you who, so budget still spreads across the wrong people inside the right logos.
- **Contact-level ABM retargeting** — reaches the named buyers inside those accounts: the six-to-eleven people on the buying committee who actually decide.


Account-level retargeting feels like ABM because the logos are right. But an account isn't a buyer. Until you know which person to reach, you're paying to retarget a company average — and averages don't click ads.


## Reach the right people, not just the right accounts


Landing on the right account is the start, not the finish. B2B buying committees run six to eleven people, and a retargeting audience built at the account level blurs them into one anonymous dot. The job is to reach the specific contacts who are researching, comparing, and deciding.


Contact-level retargeting re-serves ads to named, ICP-fit people who engaged with your brand — including the ones you'd otherwise never see. Most retargeting is capped at known contacts and form-fills, but the majority of buyers research without ever converting. And every identified contact can route to sales with a name, a behavior, and a reason to reach out, so paid retargeting and sales follow-up point at the same person.


## How contact-level ABM retargeting works


The mechanics are a loop, not a one-time list upload:


1. **Identify.** Vector identifies the buyers engaging with your site and ads — including ad engagers who never converted — by name, title, and company.
2. **Build.** Vector turns that behavior into a retargeting audience and refreshes it automatically as people research, visit, and engage.
3. **Activate.** The same ICP logic pushes that audience across LinkedIn, Google, Meta, and Reddit, so you retarget the same named people wherever they are.
4. **Coordinate.** Once a contact is identified, sales gets the name and the context, so outreach reinforces the ads instead of running blind.


Nothing here asks you to abandon your ABM stack. Account scoring and intent tools still decide which accounts matter; contact-level retargeting decides which people inside them you actually reach.


## What to retarget on: signal, not just a pixel fire


Not every visit deserves a retargeting dollar. A pixel fire tells you a browser loaded a page — it doesn't tell you a buyer is in-market. The signal you retarget on should separate real intent from noise:


- **Signal:** a named ICP contact on a high-intent page — pricing, docs, playbooks, or five-plus pages deep across the site.
- **Noise:** an anonymous single-page bounce you can't tie to a person or an account.


Two more things separate ABM retargeting that works from spend that drifts. Retarget on *live* behavior: contact-level audiences refresh as buyers move, instead of decaying like a static pixel list that keeps serving ads to people who churned out of the market months ago. And lean smaller and higher-intent — audience bloat is how retargeting budgets quietly bleed into ghost traffic. A tight audience of named, in-market buyers beats a broad one padded with anyone who ever loaded the homepage.


## Stop retargeting ghosts, start reaching buyers


The right account is where ABM starts; the right people are the point. Standard retargeting chases anyone, account-level retargeting reaches a company, and only contact-level retargeting reaches the named buyers who actually decide. ## FAQs


### What is ABM retargeting?


ABM retargeting is retargeting scoped to named, qualified contacts inside your ICP and target accounts, rather than to anyone who visited your site. It re-serves ads to the specific buyers who fit your ICP and belong to accounts you're pursuing, so spend follows real potential pipeline instead of off-ICP traffic like job seekers and competitors.


### How is ABM retargeting different from standard retargeting?


Standard retargeting chases every prior visitor regardless of fit, so most of the budget follows people who will never buy. ABM retargeting narrows to known, qualified contacts inside your target accounts. Generic retargeting chases anyone who's been to your site; contact-level retargeting focuses only on known, qualified contacts.


### What's the difference between account-level and contact-level retargeting?


Account-level retargeting reaches visitors from a target company — usually by IP or company match — but can't tell you which person, so budget spreads across the wrong people inside the right logos. Contact-level retargeting reaches the named buyers on the buying committee. Because committees run six to eleven people, the account average isn't a buyer; the specific contact is.


### Can you retarget buyers who engaged but never converted?


Yes, and that's most of them. Standard retargeting is usually capped at known contacts and form-fills, but the majority of buyers research without converting. Vector surfaces the people who engaged with your ads and never filled anything out, so they enter the retargeting pool as named contacts instead of disappearing.


### How do you measure ABM retargeting?


Measure people and pipeline, not just retargeting impressions and CTR. Cost per engaged contact and pipeline from in-tier accounts tell you whether retargeting reached real buyers and influenced revenue. If your retargeting reporting stops at reach and clicks, you can't tell qualified engagement from wasted frequency.
